trigger: Waterborne emergency, such as a failure or significant interruption in key water treatment processes (for example a chlorine overfeed or loss of disinfection reaching the distribution system), or another situation the primacy agency designates Tier 1
deadline: As soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the situation
notify: All persons served, in a form reasonably calculated to reach them, using at least one of: broadcast media, posting throughout the service area, hand delivery, or another method the primacy agency approves in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if the incident interrupted key treatment or off-target water may have reached customers. Decision: Chief Operator with the Owner and General Manager

deadline: Initiate as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the situation; then meet any added requirements from the consultation (repeat notices, duration)
notify: State drinking water primacy agency (district office; after-hours number being added, P03 G-011)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes with any Tier 1 situation. Company rule: also call the agency for any confirmed unauthorized control action even without a Tier 1 trigger

obligation: Notice that the minimum residual disinfectant was not maintained
trigger: The system does compliance monitoring under 141.403(b) and fails to meet the state-determined minimum residual disinfectant concentration, and it is not restored within 4 hours
deadline: As soon as possible, but no later than the end of the next business day
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker lowered or stopped the chlorine feed long enough to drop the entry point residual below the permit minimum for more than 4 hours

obligation: Report failure to comply with a drinking water regulation
trigger: The incident causes a violation of a national primary drinking water regulation, including a monitoring failure (for example grab samples not taken every 4 hours while the continuous residual record was lost, 141.403(b)(3)(i)(A))
deadline: Within 48 hours, unless the part sets a different period

trigger: Completion of the initial public notice and any repeat notices
deadline: Within 10 days of completing the public notification requirements, with a representative copy of each type of notice

obligation: Keep copies of public notices and certifications

citation: 42 U.S.C. 300i-1 (tampering, attempting or threatening to tamper with a public water system is a federal crime)
trigger: Evidence that someone interfered or tried to interfere with the operation of the system
deadline: No statutory reporting deadline. Company rule (POL-03 4.7): within 24 hours of declaring the incident
notify: FBI field office (or IC3 online report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for any confirmed unauthorized control action. Preserve evidence for investigators

citation: Voluntary. No federal mandatory cyber incident reporting rule applied to this water system as of 2026-09-25
deadline: Company rule (POL-03 4.7): within 24 hours of declaration
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary). Full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is also a mitigating factor for OFAC if a ransom is ever considered

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No. Final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed, the company would not be covered: it is under the SBA size standard and serves 2,850 persons, not more than 3,300. Recheck when a final rule is published and if the population served passes 3,300 (growth watch item)

trigger: Breach of security of customer or employee personal information (for example customer portal user names with passwords, or bank draft account details where breach counsel finds they meet the definition in 501.171(1)(g)) if the attacker reached the billing, payroll, or email systems
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 more days are available if good cause is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); law enforcement delay allowed on written request
notify: Affected Florida residents (written notice or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed. An HMI compromise alone does not trigger it; the MSP and forensics confirm in analysis whether office systems were reached

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida (the billing system holds 1,190 customer accounts)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. The 15-day good-cause extension does not apply to this notice
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Floridians' personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified (possible if all customer accounts were exposed)

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains customer or employee personal information for the company (billing vendor, payroll vendor, MSP) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable but no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Added to vendor contracts by 2026-12-31 (POL-02 A.5; POL-03 4.8)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed and some affected customers or former employees live outside Florida (for example seasonal residents with out-of-state billing addresses). Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. Applies if the HMI incident turns into extortion

citation: Cyber liability policy in force since 2025-11-01 (contract)
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice; call the 24x7 breach hotline before hiring outside vendors and use panel vendors

obligation: Contractor incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: Contract addenda for the SCADA integrator, MSP, and remote monitoring vendor (POL-02 A.5; due 2026-12-31)
trigger: A security incident at the contractor or vendor that affects company systems, the remote desktop tool, or company files (including the integrator's copy of the PLC program)
deadline: Within 24 hours (once the addenda are signed; no notice duty exists today)
notify: The company (Chief Operator and Office Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes once the addenda are signed. Until then the company relies on goodwill (P03 G-027)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
